meaning:
συμ-φέρω
[in LXX: Jer.33:14 (טוֹב), Pro.19:10 (נָאוֶה), Sir.30:19, al. ;]
1. trans. to bring together: with accusative of thing(s), Act.19:19.
2. Intrans., and mostly impers., συμφέρει, it is expedient, profitable or an advantage: 1Co.6:12 10:23, 2Co.8:10; with inf. (M, Pr., 210), Mat.19:10, Jhn.18:14; with dative, before ἵνα (Bl., § 69, 5), Mat.5:29-30 18:6, Jhn.11:50 16:7. Ptcp., ςυμφέρων, profitable: 1Co.12:7; pl., Act.20:20; (οὐ σ. sc. ἐστιν; = οὐ συμφέρει; cf. Thuc., iii, 44, 2), 2Co.12:1; as subst., τὸ σ., profit, Heb.12:10.†
(AS)

renderings.bsb: Although there is nothing to gain

elsewhere.note: If your right eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it away from you. For it is more profitable for you that one of your members should perish…
nor do you consider that it is advantageous for us that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation not perish.”
Many of those who practiced magical arts brought their books together and burned them in the sight of all. They counted their price, and found it to be fifty…
“All things are lawful for me,” but not all things are expedient. “All things are lawful for me,” but I will not be brought under the power of anything.
I give a judgment in this: for this is expedient for you who were the first to start a year ago, not only to do, but also to be willing.
For they indeed, for a few days, punished us as seemed good to them; but he for our profit, that we may be partakers of his holiness.
